inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted-average shares, Q3 FY2026 10-Q (quarter ended 2026-06-30), 111.6M; cover-page basic count 111.05M. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging dilution as well would double-count). Rockwell is an active repurchaser ($754M in 9M FY2026, $425M FY2025), so the flat count is funded, not a convention.
inputs.debt_note: Total debt at 2026-06-30 (SEC XBRL, Q3 FY2026 10-Q) = short-term borrowings / commercial paper 686 + current long-term debt 2 + long-term debt 2,570. The Metrics.csv TotalDebt column (2,572 at Q2 FY2026) omits commercial paper; this DCF uses the full figure. Operating lease liabilities (355 at 2026-06-30) excluded: US GAAP operating lease cost already sits inside operating income/EBITDA (treatment B by construction).
inputs.reported_fcf_basis: TTM to 2026-06-30: FY2025 FCF 1,358 + 9M FY2026 1,099 - 9M FY2025 953 = 1,504 (OCF less capex, after interest paid).
inputs.interest_income_note: TTM interest income ~$12M not stripped: Rockwell is net-debt (2.8B), so no cash pile is added to EV and the double-count rule does not apply.
inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL ShareBasedCompensation (cash-flow add-back): FY2025 85.0, 9M FY2026 69.0, 9M FY2025 65.0 -> TTM 89.0. No separate tax-withholding-on-net-share-settlement tag is filed; Rockwell's equity awards are largely options settled for cash proceeds ($93M 9M FY2026), so equity-award taxes are immaterial and not added.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST), beta ~1.1 for a large-cap quality industrial, ERP 4.5-5% -> cost of equity ~9.3%; debt ~6% of capital at ~4.5% pre-tax (3.6% after tax) -> WACC ~9.0%. Held identical across scenarios: cyclicality is priced in the scenario flows (bear carries an FY2023-24 style destock), not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: lease cost is inside operating income and EBITDA already (treatment B); lease liabilities excluded from net debt; lease_cost_pct_path 0 to avoid a second charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interest fell to $2M at 2026-06-30 after the Sensia JV exit (57 at FY2025, 165 at Q3 FY2025); immaterial, no deduction.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (routing table row 'Operating company, cyclical: industrials'), 10-year horizon, scenario-weighted, end-of-year discounting. First valuation of ROK (no MEMORY.md entry). FY0 is FY2026E rather than FY2025 because the fiscal year closed 2026-09-30 two days before this valuation and the 10-K is not yet filed: base_revenue 9,050 = FY2025 8,342 x 1.085 (midpoint of the raised 7.5-9.5% sales-growth guide; TTM to June 8,973 corroborates). Year 1 is FY2027. FY0 component check: pre-SBC EBITDA (GAAP operating income + D&A + SBC) 27.4% in 9M FY2026 vs 25.3% FY2025 and 25.0% at the FY2023 prior peak; the step-up is Software & Control mix (segment margin ~30%) plus price. Q4 FY2026 cash generation between the 2026-06-30 balance sheet and the valuation date is not credited (conservative, roughly offset by Q4 buybacks/dividends). Pension: noncurrent pension/OPEB liability 406 at 2026-06-30 deducted after 21% tax in the equity bridge. Working capital is negative capture (receivables + inventory exceed payables + contract liabilities, ~14% of revenue).

equity_bridge.item: Unfunded pension and OPEB, after 21% tax

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 22.5% vs revenue 5.7% and EPS -2.7%: FY2020 book (1,347) was depressed by a decade of buybacks exceeding earnings, and FY2020-21 EPS was inflated by PTC mark-to-market gains, so neither equity nor EPS CAGR is a usable growth anchor. Revenue 5yr CAGR (includes Plex/Clearpath/Verve acquisitions) selected instead.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs end at FY2025 (last completed year). FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (FCF - SBC). The 3yr FCF CAGR of 27.5% starts from the FY2022 supply-chain inventory build trough (owner FCF 614) and is not a forward rate; the 5yr 5.8% is the cleaner read. Owner-FCF CAGR is only ~0.4pp below reported, so SBC (~1% of revenue) is not consuming the growth.

base.narrative: Recovery runs through FY2027-28, then a mild mid-cycle pause (FY2029-30) before trend growth of ~4-5% fading to 3%; margin settles at ~27.5% pre-SBC EBITDA, holding the software-mix gain but not extending it.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: Year 1 trimmed to 27.6% so the FY2027 unlevered owner-FCF margin (~18%) sits only modestly above the FY2026E run-rate (~17.5%: guided ~100% conversion of ~$1.48B adjusted income, plus after-tax interest); settles at 27.5%, holding the FY2026 software-mix gain.

scenario_narratives.base: The FY2025-26 recovery (organic +10% in Q3 FY2026, two guidance raises) is real but cyclical: restocking and data-centre/semiconductor capex carry FY2027-28, then discrete-manufacturing capex pauses as it has every 4-5 years, before reshoring and the software mix restore ~4-5% growth fading to 3%. Software & Control's margin gains (segment ~30%) are kept but not extended; Lifecycle Services stays flat-ish and Intelligent Devices remains a hardware cyclical. Capex runs above history through FY2029 on the $2B five-year US manufacturing and digital-infrastructure programme.
scenario_narratives.bull: Reshoring and tariff-driven factory investment turn into a multi-year North American automation cycle with no meaningful downturn inside the horizon; AI-enabled FactoryTalk/digital-twin software and recurring ARR lift Software & Control to ~30% of sales at low-30s margins, taking enterprise pre-SBC EBITDA to ~31%. Rockwell takes share from Siemens/Schneider in North American discrete and its installed-base switching costs convert the growth into durable aftermarket revenue.
scenario_narratives.bear: The current upswing proves to be restocking: as in FY2023-24, distributors destock and manufacturing PMI rolls over, revenue falls ~9% over FY2028-29 and margins give back the software-mix gains under negative operating leverage. Tariff and export-control volatility, China overcapacity and the larger diversified rivals' pricing keep recovery growth to 3-5% and the terminal margin at ~25.5%, below today's level, valued at a 13x cyclical exit.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% from the 15% house default because Rockwell's revenue has a demonstrated 4-5 year boom-bust pattern (FY2021-22 boom, FY2023-24 destock) and the valuation date sits after two guidance raises, i.e. later in the upswing, not at a trough. Base 50% embeds one mild pause. Bull cut to 25% from 35% because it needs several independent things at once: no cyclical downturn for a decade, sustained reshoring capex, and software mix lifting enterprise margin ~3pp.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Rockwell is valued as a quality cyclical on an owner-FCF basis: SBC (~1% of revenue) fully expensed, share count flat and funded by buybacks, mid-cycle rather than peak margins capitalised at a 13-19x exit. The market price capitalises roughly 33x trailing owner FCF, which the model can only reach if the bull case's decade without a downturn and structural margin step-up both happen; the gap between price and weighted value is the price of that thesis.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cycle timing: a FY2027-28 destock (bear) versus continued recovery swings near-term FCF by 25-30%
Software & Control margin durability: each 1pp of terminal EBITDA margin is worth roughly 4% of value
Terminal multiple: the cap binds in the base case, so a market willing to pay 20x+ for automation exposure sits outside the house basis
The $2B five-year US investment programme lifts capex above the 2.2-2.8% history; if it fails to earn a return, base FCF is overstated
Tariff/IEEPA refunds and export controls on industrial control technology to China
